channel.title: Geneticapedia
channel.description: News, explainers and frequently asked questions about genetics, without the jargon.

item.title: KJ, the first baby treated with bespoke gene editing
item.description: In 2025 a Philadelphia team designed, in six months, a gene edit for a single baby with a deadly metabolic disease. A milestone that could change how rare diseases are treated.

item.title: Casgevy, the first approved CRISPR therapy
item.description: Three years ago the United Kingdom approved the first CRISPR-based medicine, for sickle cell disease and beta-thalassaemia. What it does, who it helps and why it still reaches few patients.

item.title: Geneticapedia is born
item.description: Why an encyclopedia of genetics written by a family doctor, and what you will find in it.

item.title: Avery, MacLeod and McCarty: DNA is the hereditary material
item.description: In 1944, nine years before the double helix, three researchers in New York showed that genes are made of DNA. The story behind our cover photo.

item.title: Rosalind Franklin and "Photo 51"
item.description: The scientist whose X-ray images were key to discovering the double helix, and whose contribution took decades to be recognised.

item.title: Do we share 60 % of our DNA with a banana?
item.description: A figure that circulates everywhere and that, as usually told, is not true. What it really means.
